questions.q: A series LCR circuit is subjected to an ac signal of $200 \mathrm{~V}, 50 \mathrm{~Hz}$. If the voltage across the inductor $(\mathrm{L}=10 \mathrm{mH})$ is $31.4 \mathrm{~V}$, then the current in this circuit is _____ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Voltage across inductor } \mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{L}}=\mathrm{IX}_{\mathrm{L}} \\ & 31.4=\mathrm{I}[\mathrm{L} \omega] \\ & 31.4=\mathrm{I}[\mathrm{L}(2 \pi \mathrm{f})] \\ & 31.4=\mathrm{I}\left[10 \times 10^{-3}(2 \times 3.14) \times 50\right. \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{I}=10 \mathrm{~A}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: When you walk through a metal detector carrying a metal object in your pocket, it raises an alarm. This phenomenon works on
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Metal detector works on the principle of transmitting an electromagnetic signal and analyses a return signal from the target. So it works on the principle of resonance in $AC$& circuit.

When the LC circuit detects any resonating frequency from any metal which is near to it, electric field will be created which will lead to induces current in the coil and changes in the signal flow through the coil.

questions.q: A circuit element $X$ when connected to an AC~supply of peak voltage $100V$ gives a peak current of $5A$ which is in phase with the voltage. A second element $Y$ when connected to the same AC~supply also gives the same value of peak current which lags behind the voltage by $\dfrac{π}{2}$. If $X$ and $Y$ are connected in series to the same supply, what will be the rms value of the current in ampere?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As current is in phase with the applied voltage, element $X$ should be resistive with $R = \dfrac{V0}{I0} = \dfrac{100}{5} = 20Ω$.

As current lags behind voltage by~$90 °$, element $Y$ should be inductive with ${X}_{L} = \dfrac{V0}{I0} = \dfrac{100}{5} = 20Ω$

When $X$ and $Y$ are connector in series,~

Impedance,~$Z = \sqrt{{X}_L^{2} + R^{2}} = \sqrt{{20}^{2} + {20}^{2}} = 20\sqrt{2}Ω$

Now, peak current,~${I}_{0} = \dfrac{V0}{Z} = \dfrac{100}{20\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{5}{2}A$

Thus, the rms value of current is~${I}_{rms} = \dfrac{I0}{2} = \dfrac{5}{2}A$

questions.q: A coil of negligible resistance is connected in series with $90 \Omega$ resistor across $120 \mathrm{~V}, 60 \mathrm{~Hz}$ supply. A voltmeter reads $36 \mathrm{~V}$ across resistance. Inductance of the coil is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & 36=I_{\mathrm{rms}} \mathrm{R} \\ & 36=\frac{120}{\sqrt{\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{L}}^2+\mathrm{R}^2}} \times \mathrm{R} \\ & \mathrm{R}=90 \Omega \Rightarrow 36=\frac{120 \times 90}{\sqrt{\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{L}}^2+90^2}} \\ & \sqrt{\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{L}}^2+90^2}=300 \\ & \mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{L}}^2=81900 \\ & \mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{L}}=286.18 \\ & \omega \mathrm{L}=286.18 \\ & \mathrm{~L}=\frac{286.18}{376.8} \\ & \mathrm{~L}=0.76 \mathrm{H}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: $AC$ voltage $V ( t ) = 20sin\omegat$~of frequency $50$ Hz is applied to a parallel plate capacitor. The separation between the plates is $2$ mm and the area is $1m^{2}$. The amplitude of the oscillating displacement current for the applied $AC$ voltage is  \left[\text{Take}{ε}_{0} = 8 . 85 \times {10}^{- 12}Fm^{- 1}\right]$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From the given information,

$C = \dfrac{{∈}_{0}A}{d} = \dfrac{{ϵ}_{0} \times 1}{2 \times {10}^{- 3}}F$
$∴ {X}_{C} = \dfrac{1}{\omegaC} = \dfrac{2 \times {10}^{- 3}}{2 \times 50\pi \times {∈}_{0}} = \dfrac{2 \times {10}^{- 3}}{25 \times 4\pi{∈}_{0}}Ω$
$∴ {X}_{C} = \dfrac{2 \times {10}^{- 3}}{25} \times 9 \times {10}^{9} = \dfrac{18}{25} \times {10}^{6}Ω$
$∴ {i}_{0} = \dfrac{V0}{XC} = \dfrac{20 \times 25}{18} \times {10}^{- 6}A = 27 . 47\text{\mu A} .$

The value of amplitude of displacement current will be same as value of amplitude of conventional current.
Hence option $3 .$

Impedance of the given LCR circuit will be,& $Z = \sqrt{R^{2} + \left({X}_{L} - {X}_{C}\right)2} ⇒ Z = \sqrt{{100}^{2} + \left(200 - 100\right)2}$

questions.q: A direct current of $4A$ and an alternating current of peak value $4A$~flow through resistance of $3Ω$ and $2Ω$ respectively. The ratio of heat produced in the two resistances in same interval of time will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Heat produced in resistor when direct current flows is& ${H}_{1} = i^{2}{R}_{1}t$~ ~

${H}_{1} = {4}^{2}\left(3\right)t = 16\left(3\right)t$

Heat produced in resistor when alternating current flows is ${H}_{2} = {i}_{rms}^{2}{R}_{2}t\left\{{i}_{rms} = \dfrac{i0}{2}\right\}$

${H}_{2} = {i}_{0}^{2}2{R}_{2}t$

${H}_{2} = \dfrac{42}{2} \times \left(2\right)t = 16t$

Thus, the ratio is~${H}_{1}: {H}_{2} = 3: 1$

questions.q: For the given circuit the current $i$ through the battery when the key in closed and the steady state has been reached is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
In a steady state, the inductor behaves as a conducting wire. So, the equivalent circuit becomes,&

$\dfrac{1}{Req} = \dfrac{1}{R1} + \dfrac{1}{R2} + \dfrac{1}{R3} = \dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{3} = 1 ⇒ {R}_{eq} = 1Ω$

so, the circuit becomes,~

$⇒ I = \dfrac{30}{3} = 10A$

questions.q: An alternating emf $E = 440sin100\pit$ is applied~to a circuit containing an inductance of $\dfrac{2}{π}H$. If an a.c. ammeter is connected in the circuit, its reading will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given that& $E = 440sin100\pit, L = \dfrac{2}{π}H$

Angular frequency of the source is~$\omega = 100\pirads^{- 1}$.

Now the reactance of the inductor will be,

${X}_{L} = \omegaL = 100\pi\dfrac{2}{π} = 100\sqrt{2}Ω$

Therefore, the peak current ${I}_{0} = \dfrac{E0}{XL} = \dfrac{440}{100\sqrt{2}} = 2 . 2\sqrt{2}A$

$AC$ ammeter reads RMS value therefore reading will be ${I}_{rms}$

${I}_{rms} = \dfrac{I0}{2} = 2 . 2A$

questions.q: The RMS& value of conduction current in a parallel plate capacitor is $6 . 9\muA$. The capacity of this capacitor, if it is connected to $230V$~AC~supply with an angular frequency of $600rads^{- 1}$, will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
${I}_{rms} = 6 . 9\mu A; {V}_{rms} = 230V; \omega = 600rads^{- 1}$

Current in capacitor ${I}_{rms} = \dfrac{Vrms}{XC}$, where,~${X}_{C}$~is~capacitive reactance given by~${X}_{C} = \dfrac{1}{\omegaC}$

Now, current,~${I}_{rms} = \left({V}_{rms}\right) \times\left(\omegaC\right)

So, capacitance is~$C = $\dfrac{Irms}{{V}_{rms}\omega} = \dfrac{6 . 9 \times {10}^{- 6}}{230 \times 600} =$50pF$

$

questions.q: An LCR circuit is at resonance for a capacitor $C$, inductance $L$ and resistance $R$. Now the value of resistance is halved keeping all other parameters same. The current amplitude at resonance will be now:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
In resonance $Z=R\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{I}=\frac{\mathrm{V}}{\mathrm{R}} \\ & \mathrm{R} \rightarrow \text { halved } \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{I} \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{I}\end{aligned}$
I becomes doubled.

questions.q: A $10Ω$ resistance is connected across~$220V - 50Hz$~AC supply. The time taken by the current to change from its maximum value to the $r$ ms value is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$⇒ i = {i}_{0}sin\omegat$

When $i = {i}_{0}$

${i}_{0} = {i}_{0}sin\omega{t}_{1} ⇒ \omega{t}_{1} = \dfrac{π}{2} \ldots ( 1 )$

When~$i = \dfrac{i0}{2}$

$\dfrac{i0}{2} = {i}_{0}sin\omega{t}_{2} ⇒ \omega{t}_{2} = \dfrac{π}{4} \ldots ( 2 )$

Time taken by current from maximum value to rms value,~$⇒ \left({t}_{1} - {t}_{2}\right) = \dfrac{π}{2\omega} - \dfrac{π}{4\omega} = \dfrac{π}{4\omega} = \dfrac{π}{4 \times 2\pif}$

$= \dfrac{1}{8 \times 50}$

$= \dfrac{1}{400}sec$

$= 2 . 5ms$

questions.q:
A coil of inductance $1H$ and resistance $100Ω$ is connected to a battery of $6V$. Determine approximately :

(a) The time elapsed before the current acquires half of its steady-state~value
(b) The energy stored in the magnetic field associated with the coil at an instant $15$ ms after the circuit is switched on. (Given $ln2 = 0 . 693$, $e\dfrac{- 3}{2} = 0 . 25$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given circuit is $R - L$ growth circuit

The current is the circuit is given by,~

$i = \dfrac{E}{R} \left(1 - e^{- $\dfrac{t}{τ}}\right)$

For current to be half of the peak value,

$i = $\dfrac{E}{2R} = \dfrac{E}{R} \left(1 - e^{- $\dfrac{t}{τ}}\right)$

Solving $t = τln2$

$t = $\dfrac{L}{R}$ln2 = $\dfrac{1}{100}$0 . 693 = 0 . 00693≃ 7ms$

At time~$t = 15ms$,

$i \left(15ms\right) = \dfrac{E}{R} \left($1 - e^{- \dfrac{15}{10}}\right)$

$⇒ i = \dfrac{6}{100}\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{4}\right) = \dfrac{3}{4} \times \dfrac{6}{100} =0 . 045A$

$⇒ U = \dfrac{1}{2}Li^{2}$

by solving we get $U = 1mJ.

$

questions.q: In series LCR circuit, the capacitance is changed from $C$ to $4C$. To keep the resonance frequency unchanged, the new inductance should be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As resonance frequency remains unchanged, therefore $\omega ' = \omega$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{L ' C '} = \dfrac{1}{LC}$

$⇒ L ' C ' = LC$

$⇒ L ' \left(4C\right) = LC$

$⇒ L ' = \dfrac{L}{4}$

$∵$ Inductance must be decreased by $\dfrac{3L}{4}$.

questions.q: An ac source is connected in given series LCR circuit. The rms potential difference across the capacitor of $20 \mu \mathrm{F}$ is _____V.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{L}}=\omega \mathrm{L}=100 \times 1=100 \Omega \\ & \mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{C}}=\frac{1}{\omega \mathrm{C}}=\frac{1}{100 \times 20 \times 10^{-6}}=500 \Omega \\ & \mathrm{Z}=\sqrt{\left(\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{L}}-\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{C}}\right)^2+\mathrm{R}^2} \\ & \sqrt{(100-500)^2+300^2} \\ & \mathrm{Z}=500 \Omega \\ & \mathrm{i}_{\text {rms }}=\frac{\mathrm{V}_{\text {rms }}}{\mathrm{Z}}=\frac{50}{500}=0.1 \mathrm{~A} \\ & \text { rms voltage across capacitor } \\ & \mathrm{V}_{\text {rms }}=\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{C}} \mathrm{i}_{\text {rms }} \\ & =500 \times 0.1=50 \mathrm{~V}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The alternating current is given by,& $i = \left\{\sqrt{42}sin\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{T}t\right) + 10\right\}A$. The R.M.S. value of this current is __________~$A$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The given function of current is,& $i = \left\{\sqrt{42}sin\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{T}t\right) + 10\right\}A$

It means, $i^{2} = 42\sin^{2} \left(\dfrac{2\pit}{T}\right) +$100 + 20$\sqrt{42}$sin\left(\dfrac{2\pit}{T}\right)

$⇒ \left$<i^{2}\right> = $\dfrac{42}{2} +$100$

RMS value of the current is,~${i}_{rms} = $\sqrt{\left<i^{2}\right>} = \sqrt{121} =$11A$

$

questions.q: A $110V, 50Hz, AC$ source is connected in the circuit (as shown in figure). The current through the resistance $55Ω$, at resonance in the circuit, will be _____A.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let current in the inductance is& ${i}_{L}$,~through the capacitor is~${i}_{C}$~and through resistance is~${i}_{R}$~at any instance as shown in the figure.

According to the Kirchoff's junction law,~${i}_{R} = {i}_{L} + {i}_{C}$.

At resonance~${X}_{C} = {X}_{L}$~hence ${i}_{L} = {i}_{C}$. Also, current through the capacitor and inductor have phase difference of~$\pirad$. Therefore, they will form destructive interference and hence the current through the resistance will be~$0$.

questions.q: A telegraph line of length $100$ km has a capacity of $0 . 01\muF{km}^{- 1}$~and it carries an alternating current at $0 . 5$~kilo cycle per second. If minimum impedance is required, then the value of the inductance that needs to be introduced in series is _____~$mH$. (If~$\pi = \sqrt{10}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The frequency given is& $0 . 5$~kilo cycle per second~$⇒ f = 500Hz ⇒ \omega = 2\pif = 1000\pirads^{- 1}$.

Total capacitance of the wire is~$C = 0 . 01 \times {10}^{- 6} \times 100F$.

Impedance is minimum at resonance. Therefore, for minimum impedance

${X}_{L} = {X}_{C}$

$⇒ \omegaL = \dfrac{1}{\omegaC} ⇒ L = \dfrac{1}{{ω}^{2}C} = \dfrac{1}{{1000}^{2} \times {π}^{2} \times 0 . 01 \times {10}^{- 6} \times 100} = {10}^{- 1}H = 100mH$
